subject: AWS Marketplace: SKU entitlement mapping + webhook design for SaaS fulfillment
messages:
From: Linda Kim <linda.kim@aws-partner.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>
Cc: Craig Taylor <craig.taylor@acmecorp.com>, Procurement <procurements@acmecorp.com>
Date: 2028-06-30T09:12:00Z
Subject: AWS Marketplace integration: SKU mapping + webhook prototype

Hi Hannah,

Thanks again for the call yesterday. Per our discussion, Acme Analytics is ready to move ahead with AWS Marketplace SaaS Fulfillment but needs the SKU <-> entitlement mapping and the metering webhook payload defined to avoid invoicing gaps during the pilot.

Attached: acme-sku-mapping-draft.csv (their current SKU list), and an initial webhook spec (aws-webhook-spec-v2.docx) that the marketplace engineering team prefers.

Two asks from our side so we can scope Redwood Dedicated fulfillment:
1) Can you confirm how Redwood will map Acme product SKUs to marketplace entitlements (seat-based vs consumption)? We need a CSV mapping example that your billing team can accept.
2) Can Redwood emit the marketplace metering events in the required namespace with the following fields: product_code, usage_dimension, quantity, timestamp, customer_reference? If not, what is the recommended adapter approach?

Also looped Craig (Acme PM) and their procurement to flag any contract amendments needed (e.g., addendum for metering/PRORATE and invoice format). If you have an initial amendment template we can review, please share.

Happy to jump on a quick design call this week.

Best,
Linda
Partner Programs, AWS Marketplace

Attachment stubs: acme-sku-mapping-draft.csv (text/csv), aws-webhook-spec-v2.docx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.wordprocessingml.document)

From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>
To: Linda Kim <linda.kim@aws-partner.com>, Craig Taylor <craig.taylor@acmecorp.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-06-30T11:04:00Z
Subject: Re: AWS Marketplace integration: SKU mapping + webhook prototype

Thanks Linda — good summary. Quick responses up front, then proposed next steps below.

1) SKU <-> entitlement mapping
We can accept both seat-based and consumption SKUs. For the pilot we prefer a one-to-one CSV mapping with columns: acme_sku, marketplace_product_code, usage_dimension, billing_type (seat|consumption), unit_multiplier, redwood_sku_id. I'll attach a short template and populate a first-pass mapping for the three pilot SKUs.

2) Metering events / webhook capability
Our serving runtime can emit marketplace metering events from the fulfillment adapter. We support a lightweight adapter that translates internal usage records to the AWS metering API schema. Key notes:
- We can include product_code, usage_dimension, quantity, timestamp, customer_reference (we use customer_reference = acme_customer_id).
- For seat-based billing we send 1-off activation events and monthly recurring entitlements; for consumption we batch events into 1-minute windows to reduce spikes.
- We will expose an inbound validation endpoint for signed AWS webhook callbacks and provide HMAC signing for outgoing events.

Attachment: acme-sku-mapping-template.csv (I will send next message with filled rows).

Proposed next steps:
- Hannah/Tam (product ops) to produce mapping CSV by EOD today for the three pilot SKUs. (cc: Marissa for fulfillment ops)
- Schedule a 45-min engineering sync with Acme + AWS to review webhook payload examples (tomorrow 10am PT suggested).
- Kimberly to draft a short amendment for SaaS Marketplace fulfillment (metering, proration, invoice format) and share a PDF for legal review.

If procurement needs a point-of-contact for invoicing changes, loop Kimberly and Marissa.

Thanks —
Hannah
Director, Marketplace Integrations
Redwood Inference

Attachment stub: acme-sku-mapping-template.csv (text/csv)

From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>
To: Linda Kim <linda.kim@aws-partner.com>, Craig Taylor <craig.taylor@acmecorp.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-06-30T12:22:00Z
Subject: Re: AWS Marketplace integration: SKU mapping + webhook prototype

On attaching the first-pass mapping — see below (CSV rendered inline for thread clarity):

acme_sku,marketplace_product_code,usage_dimension,billing_type,unit_multiplier,redwood_sku_id
ACME-CORE-001,ACME.PROD.CORE,core_hours,consumption,1,RD-SKU-0007
ACME-ANALYTICS-STD,ACME.PROD.ANALYTICS,monthly_seats,seat,1,RD-SKU-0011
ACME-EXPORTS-API,ACME.PROD.EXPORT,api_calls,consumption,1000,RD-SKU-0023

Notes on the mapping:
- The EXPORTS-API SKU is metered in API call batches; Redwood will aggregate calls per customer per minute and send quantity in units of 1000 (unit_multiplier).
- For monthly_seats we will emit an entitlement activation event at onboarding and an update event on changes.
- For core_hours we will send aggregated hourly usage with a timestamp bucket.

Attached to this message is the populated CSV and a short draft amendment (SaaS-Marketplace-Amendment-draft.pdf) that flags invoicing cadence and proration behavior. Kimberley/Marissa — please review the amendment and call out anything we should push on contract language (invoice format / settlement window).

Proposed timeslot for engineering sync: 2028-07-01 10:00 PT (45 min). Linda, please confirm and I’ll send a calendar invite.

Thanks,
Hannah

Attachment stubs: acme-sku-mapping-draft.csv, SaaS-Marketplace-Amendment-draft.pdf

From: Craig Taylor <craig.taylor@acmecorp.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>, Linda Kim <linda.kim@aws-partner.com>
Cc: Procurement <procurements@acmecorp.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-06-30T16:42:00Z
Subject: Re: AWS Marketplace integration: SKU mapping + webhook prototype

Hannah — thanks for the quick turnaround and the CSV. A few procurement/ops items from our side that will determine go/no-go for the pilot: 

1) Amendment: Our procurement team needs the SaaS Marketplace amendment to explicitly state proration rules for mid-cycle seat changes and the invoice reconciliation window (we require 30-day reconciliation). Please forward the draft to procurements@acmecorp.com for review.

2) Metering latency & reconciliation: We need an SLA on metering event delivery and a retry pattern for missed events. Can Redwood commit to a 99.9% delivery for events within a 24-hour window and provide a reconciliation API for backfill? If not, what is the realistic expectation?

3) Test plan: We want a validation run with 3 sandbox customers and an invoice preview prior to production activation. Can Redwood provide a sandbox webhook endpoint and a simulation tool / sample payloads?

If you can send the amendment and the sandbox webhook details by EOD Monday (2028-07-02), procurement will start legal review. We’re excited to get this pilot running.

Best,
Craig Taylor
Product Lead, Acme Analytics
